images.title: Two triangles fill a square
images.purpose: Shows a 5 by 5 square of dots split along a staircase into a triangle of 15 dots and a triangle of 10 dots.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large square grid of dots in the centre with a staircase dividing line and one equation below.
images.exact_structure: A 5 by 5 square of equal round dots, 25 in all, rows 1 to 5 from the top and columns 1 to 5 from the left (numbers not shown). Every dot whose column number is at most its row number is filled teal (#0072B2): rows hold 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 teal dots, 15 in all. Every other dot is filled amber (#E69F00): rows hold 4, 3, 2, 1, 0 amber dots, 10 in all. A thin dark staircase line separates the two colours. The amber triangle is tagged 10 and the teal triangle is tagged 15. Below the square, centred: 10 + 15 = 25 = 5². Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Two consecutive triangular numbers always add up to a square number.
images.description: Shows a 5 by 5 square of dots split along a staircase into a triangle of 15 dots and a triangle of 10 dots.

image_decisions.why: Fitting the two triangles into one square shows why their sum is a perfect square.
